channel.title: RNLearn
channel.description: Deep-dive guides, models, and essays across science, economics, and history

item.title: What is Science, Really? Demarcation, Revolutions, and the Fabric of Truth
item.description: From Bacon and Hume's induction to Popper's falsification, Kuhn's paradigms, Lakatos, Feyerabend, Bayesian belief, and the replication crisis.

item.title: The Strange New Physics: Relativity, the Quantum, and the Subatomic Realm
item.description: From the Michelson-Morley null result and Planck's quantum to Einstein's relativity, Rutherford's nucleus, Bohr's orbits, and Heisenberg's uncertainty.

item.title: The Clockwork Heavens and the Open Eye: The Scientific Revolution
item.description: From Copernicus and Tycho Brahe's baseline to Kepler's elliptical orbits, Galileo's telescope, Descartes, and Newton's Principia: the birth of modern physics.

item.title: The Book of Life: Evolution, the Cell, and the Code
item.description: From Linnaean taxonomy and Cuvier's fossils to Darwin, Mendel's peas, Pasteur's germ theory, and Watson-Crick-Franklin's double helix: how life came to know itself.

item.title: Mathematics Becomes Infinite: Calculus, Rigour, and the Limits of Reason
item.description: From Newton and Leibniz's calculus and the crisis of non-Euclidean geometry to Cantor's transfinite infinities, Gödel's incompleteness, and Turing's machines.

item.title: Keepers and Builders of Knowledge: Science in the Medieval Commonwealth
item.description: From Baghdad's House of Wisdom and Ibn al-Haytham's optics to Kerala's calculus, Song Dynasty clocks, and European universities: how medieval thinkers transformed science.

item.title: Gods, Stars and Calendars: The Dawn of Systematic Order
item.description: From Babylonian sexagesimal algebra and Egyptian water clocks to Indus Valley weights and Maya calendar gears: how early civilizations built systematic knowledge.

item.title: From Tally Marks to Proof: The Story of Mathematics to the Middle Ages
item.description: From Babylonian clay tablets and Euclid's axiomatic geometry to Indian zero, Brahmagupta's negative numbers, and al-Khwārizmī's algebra: how mathematics learned to prove.

item.title: From Alchemy to the Periodic Table: The Making of Chemistry
item.description: From Islamic alembics and Boyle's Sceptical Chymist to Lavoisier's oxygen balance, Dalton's atoms, and Mendeleev's periodic cathedral: the rise of chemical science.

item.title: Fire, Light and Fields: Energy, Heat and Electromagnetism in the Nineteenth Century
item.description: From Rumford's cannon-boring and Carnot's heat engine to Joule, Clausius's entropy, Faraday's lines of force, and Maxwell's electromagnetic wave equations.

item.title: Before Science: How a Curious Ape Learned to Know
item.description: From 3.3-million-year-old stone cores at Lomekwi and controlled fire to ochre symbols and lunar tally bones: how humanity built empirical knowledge before writing.

item.title: Asking "Why" Without the Gods: The Birth of Natural Philosophy
item.description: From Thales, Democritean atomism, and Aristotle's biology to Indian Vaiśeṣika physics, Nyāya logic, and Eratosthenes measuring the Earth: the rise of natural explanation.
